name: AGQA
description: We present Action Genome Question Answering (AGQA), a new benchmark for compositional spatio-temporal reasoning.

name: AGQA 2.0
description: We introduce AGQA 2.0, a version of this benchmark with several improvements, most namely a stricter balancing procedure.

name: AmbiModBench
description: We propose AmbiModBench, a specificity-aware, gene- resolved and coverage-aware benchmark.

name: AnnotateMissense
description: We present AnnotateMissense, a scalable annotation, benchmarking and genome-wide prediction framework for missense variant interpretation.

name: ASTER
description: Here, we propose ASTER, an ensemble learning- based tool for accurately estimating the number of cell types in scCAS data.

name: Benchmarking DNA Foundation Models
description: Here, we develop controlled evaluation metrics based on well-characterized nuclear and mitochondrial sequence features and curated variant sets.

name: benchNGS
description: We propose a benchmark to assess accuracy of short reads mapping based on the pre-computed global alignment of related genome sequences.

name: BEND
description: Benchmark of DNA language models on biologically meaningful genome annotation tasks -- chromatin accessibility, histone modification, CpG methylation and variant effects -- rather than on synthetic proxies.
notes: Finding worth carrying: DNA LM embeddings approach expert methods on some tasks but capture limited long-range information. `year: 2023` is the arXiv posting; the venue is ICLR 2024. No DOI -- ICLR mints none, so `paper_id` falls back to the arXiv ID per schema §2.2.

name: BioSecBench-Surveillance
description: We present BioSecBench-Surveillance, a verifiable benchmark of 100 evaluations testing whether AI agents can infer the right analysis pipeline from raw sequencing data and surveillance context.

name: DART-Eval
description: Regulatory-DNA focused evaluation suite comparing DNA language models against ab initio sequence baselines across zero-shot, probed and fine-tuned regimes.
notes: The finding that makes this the most useful benchmark in the seed: annotation-agnostic DNA LMs are inconsistent and show no compelling gain over ab initio baselines. Because it includes those baselines, it functions as a critique of the DNA LM programme as much as a benchmark of it. Its author list overlaps with ChromBPNet's through Kundaje, which is why model:chrombpnet derives as partially-independent rather than externally benchmarked.

name: Fahsbender 2025 Benchmarking Evaluation AI
description: Here, we present insights from a recent workshop that convened machine learning and computational biology experts across imaging, transcriptomics, proteomics, and genomics to tackle this gap.

name: Fitness Landscape for Antibodies 2
description: Here, we introduce the second iteration of the Fitness Landscape for Antibodies (FLAb2), the largest public therapeutic antibody design benchmark to date.

name: Fu 2026 iAODE benchmarking continuum
description: We introduce iAODE, a variational autoencoder that couples a zero-inflated negative binomial likelihood with a latent Neural ODE, low-weight Kullback- Leibler (KL) regularization, and an interpretable reconstruction bottleneck to learn generative, temporally continuous latent spaces.

name: Góes 2026 Evaluation Feature Representations
description: We present a systematic evaluation of machine learning models and feature extraction approaches to predict cancer-associated sORFs across 15 cancer types.

name: GENEB
description: Unified probing benchmark covering 40 genomic foundation models across 100 tasks in 13 functional categories, with leaderboard artifacts built by CI from reviewed submissions rather than hand-edited.
notes: The headline finding is the reason CFCR does not store scores: aggregate leaderboards are unstable, rankings vary sharply across task categories, and scale gives modest and inconsistent gains. Any single number CFCR copied here would be misleading within a release cycle. Submission-open and CI-built, so it stays current in a way a curated table cannot.

name: GenomeQA
description: We introduce GenomeQA, a benchmark designed to provide a controlled evaluation setting for general-purpose LLMs on sequence-based genome inference tasks.

name: GenoTEX
description: We propose GenoTEX as a promising resource for benchmarking and enhancing automated methods for gene expression data analysis.

name: GUANinE v1.0
description: Here we propose a genomic AI benchmark, GUANinE, for evaluating model generalization across a number of distinct genomic tasks.

name: HiFi-ST
description: Here, we propose HiFi-ST, a conditional neural field framework for continuous spatial transcriptomics modeling.

name: Ideas Have Genomes
description: We present IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a benchmark for scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation.

name: Jokisaari 2016 Benchmark Problems Numerical
description: We present the first set of benchmark problems for phase field models that are being developed by the Center for Hierarchical Materials Design (CHiMaD) and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).

name: JUMP-lite
description: Here we present Nahual, an open-source framework for reproducible model deployment, and JUMP-lite, a 92.0 GB subset of JUMP that is approximately 1,250-fold smaller, selected to cover genetic modalities and compound annotations and reduced via lossy JPEG XL compression.

name: Kang 2026 Benchmarking three simple
description: Here, we introduce two simple DNA image-derived metrics - Diffuse Signal Index (DSI)and 1-Gini - and benchmark them against the coefficient of variation (CV) as fixation-free readouts of chromatin reorganization.

name: Know-Show
description: We present Know-Show, a new benchmark designed to evaluate spatio-temporal grounded reasoning, the ability of a model to reason about actions and their semantics while simultaneously grounding its inferences in visual and temporal evidence.

name: LassoBench
description: We propose LassoBench, the first benchmark suite tailored for Weighted Lasso regression.

name: MatTools
description: Here, we propose a benchmark application to evaluate the proficiency of LLMs to answer materials science questions through the generation and safe execution of codes based on such physics-based computational materials science packages.

name: MVCBench
description: Herein, we introduce MVCBench, a comprehensive benchmarking framework for evaluating drug molecular and gene representation methods in predicting drug-induced multimodal virtual cell (MVC) phenotypes.

name: OncoTraj
description: We introduce OncoTraj, a public benchmark of 813 EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients receiving first-line osimertinib, harmonized from three real-world clinical-genomic sources: MSK-CHORD (672 patients), AACR Project GENIE BPC NSCLC (34 patients), and the FLAURA molecular-resistance supplement (107 patients).

name: Plato-Bio
description: We developed Plato-Bio, a biology-routed extension of the open Plato/Denario architecture that couples explicit workflow states with provenance records, citation checks, claim-to- evidence links, scoped file writes, and publication gates.

name: RegDesign-Bench
description: Here, we introduce RegDesign-Bench, a standardized framework for evaluating cell-type-specific cis-regulatory element design through a comprehensive set of computational analyses.

name: Rindtorff 2019 Biologically Plausible Benchmark
description: Here, we propose a benchmark dataset to evaluate contextual bandit algorithms based on real in vitro drug response of approximately 900 cancer cell lines.

name: Sun 2025 benchmark guide sequence-function
description: Here, we introduce a comprehensive benchmark framework for evaluating sequence-to-function models.

name: Table2Vec
description: We introduce a neural encoder Table2Vec for automated universal representation learning of entities such as customers from all-round enterprise DNA with automated data characteristics analysis and data quality augmentation.

name: HOCOMOCO v12
description: We present a major update of the HOCOMOCO collection that provides DNA binding specificity patterns of 949 human transcription factors and 720 mouse orthologs.

name: JASPAR 2024
description: Open-access database of curated, non-redundant transcription factor binding profiles stored as position frequency matrices, with taxonomic coverage across six groups and an API and bulk downloads.
notes: `year: 2023` is the Nucleic Acids Research issue year for the release branded "JASPAR 2024" -- the release name and the publication year disagree, which is normal for the NAR database issue and a recurring trap when citing these. The name is kept as the community uses it.

name: Borzoi training intervals
description: The genomic intervals and train/validation/test fold assignments used to train Borzoi, released as TSV for human and mouse.
notes: Catalogued separately from model:borzoi because fold assignment is what makes an independent evaluation comparable. Anyone benchmarking against Borzoi who re-splits the genome themselves is not measuring the same thing. Record counts are deliberately null: the source release reports 55,497 human and 49,369 mouse intervals, which is two numbers and one `n_records` column, and neither figure was confirmable from the repository metadata.

name: Dixit 2016 Perturb-seq
description: Here, we develop Perturb-seq, combining single-cell RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based perturbations to perform many such assays in a pool.

name: Enformer training intervals
description: The genomic intervals and fold assignments used to train Enformer, released as TSV for human and mouse.
notes: Same reasoning as dataset:borzoi-data. Useful mainly for like-for-like comparison against the Enformer line; the source release reports 38,171 human and 33,521 mouse intervals, again unconfirmed from repository metadata.

name: Norman 2019 combinatorial Perturb-seq
description: Here, we present an analytical framework for interpreting high-dimensional landscapes of cell states (manifolds) constructed from transcriptional phenotypes.

name: Replogle 2022 genome-scale Perturb-seq atlas
description: Genome-scale Perturb-seq screens in human cell lines, knocking down essentially all expressed genes and reading out single-cell transcriptomes, providing the reference training and evaluation data for perturbation response models.
notes: Catalogued on the `what` axis as the dataset that most perturbation models in the adjacent literature are trained or evaluated on, including model:gears. CFCR holds the pointer; the Stegle catalogue holds the method landscape.

name: Roadmap Epigenomics
description: Here we describe the integrative analysis of 111 reference human epigenomes generated as part of the programme, profiled for histone modification patterns, DNA accessibility, DNA methylation and RNA expression.

name: sci-Plex
description: Here, we introduce "sci-Plex," which uses "nuclear hashing" to quantify global transcriptional responses to thousands of independent perturbations at single-cell resolution.

name: Akita
description: Here we present a convolutional neural network, Akita, that accurately predicts genome folding from DNA sequence alone.

name: Ali 2026 Causal dictionary learning
description: We introduce a framework that combines sparse dictionary learning with causal intervention to extract, validate, and causally test interpretable features in genomic foundation models.

name: AlphaGenome
description: Unified DNA sequence model taking 1 Mb of input and predicting thousands of functional genomic tracks at base resolution across multiple modalities, covering regulatory variant effect prediction in one model rather than a per-assay family.
notes: The only api-only entry in the seed, and the reason that tier exists: there are no weights to download and no license to read, so reproducibility and long-term availability rest on Google continuing to serve the endpoint. Independently evaluated for fine-mapping reproducibility by Sweeney & Kang alongside Borzoi, Enformer and Sei.

name: ARSENAL
description: We introduce ARSENAL , a short-context masked DNA language model pretrained on ENCODE candidate cis-regulatory elements.

name: Balcı 2023 intrinsically interpretable neural
description: Here, we introduce a deep learning architecture called totally interpretable sequence-to-function model (tiSFM). tiSFM improves upon the performance of standard multilayer convolutional models while using fewer parameters.

name: BarcodeBERT
description: We introduce BarcodeBERT, a family of models tailored to biodiversity analysis and trained exclusively on data from a reference library of 1.5M invertebrate DNA barcodes.

name: Barethiya 2026 Overcoming extrapolation challenges
description: We propose that incorporating the physics of protein interactions and dynamics can be an effective approach to overcome the extrapolation limitations.

name: Basenji
description: Here, we develop a machine-learning system to predict cell-type- specific epigenetic and transcriptional profiles in large mammalian genomes from DNA sequence alone.

name: Basset
description: We introduce the open source package Basset to apply CNNs to learn the functional activity of DNA sequences from genomics data.

name: Bhattacharya 2026 Elucidating Design Space
description: We introduce ExpressionVAE (eVAE), a discrete-latent perturbation model that compresses each cell into a short sequence of discrete codes through a finite-scalar-quantization (FSQ) bottleneck and trains a perturbation-conditioned discrete prior over those codes.

name: BioM-JEPA
description: Here we present BioM-JEPA, a joint- embedding predictive architecture that instead predicts aggregate representations of graph-connected gene blocks defined by protein- association and corpus-derived coexpression evidence.

name: Borzoi
description: Predicts cell-type- and tissue-specific RNA-seq coverage from DNA sequence over a 524 kb context, scoring variant effects across transcription, splicing and polyadenylation from the one model. Successor to Enformer with finer output resolution and RNA-seq heads.
notes: `year: 2023` is the first public release (bioRxiv); the Nature Genetics paper carries a 2025 issue year. Trained with the Baskerville framework rather than the Enformer codebase, so the two are not drop-in comparable despite the lineage.

name: BPNet
description: We introduce a deep learning model, BPNet, that uses DNA sequence to predict base-resolution chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-nexus binding profiles of pluripotency TFs.

name: Caduceus
description: Here, we propose an architecture motivated by these challenges that builds off the long- range Mamba block, and extends it to a BiMamba component that supports bi-directionality, and to a MambaDNA block that additionally supports RC equivariance.

name: CaLMFlow
description: We introduce CaLMFlow (Causal Language Models for Flow Matching), a novel framework that casts flow matching as a Volterra integral equation (VIE), leveraging the power of large language models (LLMs) for continuous data generation.

name: Cao 2021 Chromatin interaction neural
description: We develop a computational method, chromatin interaction neural network (ChINN), to predict chromatin interactions between open chromatin regions using only DNA sequences.

name: Carbon
description: We present C arbon , a family of efficient generative DNA language models designed as a practical reference point for this setting.

name: CellScientist
description: We present CellScientist, a protocol-constrained workflow that converts execution and validation feedback into auditable model-revision trajectories.

name: CENO
description: Here we introduce CENO, a family of long-context generative genomic world models designed to preserve local DNA grammar while extending usable context to regulatory and chromatin scales.

name: Chang 2026 Single-cell Multiome Chromatin
description: Here, we present the first single-cell multiome atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight basal ganglia regions from neurotypical adult human donors.

name: Chao 2025 Predicting dynamic expression
description: We introduce a masked DNA language model pretrained on 165 fungal genomes closely related to budding yeast that captures conserved regulatory grammar.

name: Chapman 2017 evolution logic circuits
description: We describe a novel method for contact map prediction that uses the evolution of logic circuits.

name: ChromBPNet
description: Base-resolution model of chromatin accessibility profiles that factorizes out assay-specific enzyme bias, letting learned cis-regulatory sequence syntax and TF motif contributions be read off the prediction directly.
notes: Narrow input window compared with the Enformer/Borzoi line -- it models local accessibility syntax rather than long-range regulation, which is why it answers a different `where` question despite sharing the axis. Evaluated as an ab initio baseline in DART-Eval, whose author list overlaps with this one through Kundaje, so the derivation should land it at `partially-independent` rather than `externally-benchmarked`.

name: Cunningham 2025 Generative design construction
description: Here, we develop an end-to-end pipeline for generative design of Escherichia coli plasmid backbones, from large-scale data curation through fine-tuning, sampling, bioinformatic assessment, and candidate selection.

name: DanioDecima
description: We present DanioDecima, a zebrafish-specific model leveraging transfer learning from human and mouse-trained models to predict tissue- and cell-type-specific gene expression during zebrafish embryogenesis.

name: Debnath 2026 Inference spatial chromatin
description: Here, we present ISON (Integrated Spatial Omics Network), a unified computational method for integrative spatial multi-omics analysis from single cell multiome data and spatial transcriptomics data.

name: DECANT
description: We developed DECANT to learn mechanism-aligned perturbation representations that remain stable across context shifts while preserving response fidelity.

name: DeepCis
description: Here, we introduce DeepCis, a Transformer-based multi-omics framework that integrates base-level genomic sequence and epigenomics features, as well as region-level 3D chromatin organization to capture regulatory information across multiple scales.

name: DeepGEP
description: Here, we developed DeepGEP, an attention-based Long Short-Term Memory model trained on 228 datasets, including RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and ChIP-seq of four histone modifications (H3K4me3, H3K4me1, H3K27ac, H3K27me3) from humans, pigs, and cattle.

name: DeepSCENIC
description: Here, we present DeepSCENIC, a deep learning framework that enables causal GRN inference by performing transfer learning from S2F models to single-cell multiome atlases.

name: DeepWheat
description: We present DeepWheat, a broadly applicable deep learning framework comprising DeepEXP and DeepEPI, for accurate, tissue-specific gene expression prediction.

name: Dickmänken 2026 Evaluating single-cell ATAC-seq
description: We introduce HyDrop v2, an improved custom droplet scATAC-seq method, and perform the first benchmark of scATAC-seq platforms focusing on its capacity to train S2F models and its capacity to yield TF footprints in different species.

name: Diversity by Design
description: We introduce differentially expressed gene (DEG)-aware metrics, weighted mean-squared error (WMSE) and weighted delta $R^{2}$ ($R^{2}_{w}(Δ)$) with respect to all perturbations, that measure error in niche signals with high sensitivity.

name: DNACHUNKER
description: We introduce DNAChunker, a masked DNA language model that incorporates a learnable adaptive segmentation module to produce context-dependent, variable-length units.

name: DoFormer
description: We present DoFormer , a causal multimodal Transformer that makes no DAG assumptions and leverages rich perturbational data to accurately predict previously unseen perturbations.

name: Driessen 2025 single-cell perturbation modeling
description: Here, we propose the Conditional Monge Gap which learns OT maps conditionally on arbitrary covariates.

name: DrivR-Base
description: We describe the resource's development, practical applications, and potential for future expansion and enhancement.

name: DrugPT
description: Here, we propose DrugPT, a novel Transformer-based framework for predicting gene expression changes upon drug treatment.

name: Enformer
description: Predicts gene expression and chromatin tracks from DNA sequence by combining dilated convolutions with transformer blocks, integrating regulatory information from up to 100 kb away. Established the long-context interval model as the dominant architecture for sequence-to-function prediction.
notes: The reference point the whole interval-model literature argues with. Two independent Nature Genetics analyses (Tang/Toneyan/Koo and Huang et al.) found it explains personal transcriptome variation poorly despite strong cross-locus accuracy -- the across-individual vs across-gene distinction is the single most important caveat to communicate to anyone picking it up. Replicate checkpoints and the many community ports are deliberately not separate entities; see model:flashzoi for one that is.

name: EpiExpr
description: We introduce EpiExpr, a flexible deep learning framework that predicts gene expression from 1D epigenetic tracks (EpiExpr-1D) and integrates 3D chromatin interactions (EpiExpr-3D) to capture distal regulatory effects.

name: Evo
description: We present Evo, a long-context genomic foundation model with a frontier architecture trained on millions of prokaryotic and phage genomes, and report scaling laws on DNA to complement observations in language and vision.

name: Evo 2
description: Genome language model trained on 3 trillion DNA base pairs spanning all domains of life, with 7B and 40B parameter variants, a 1 million token context window at single-nucleotide resolution, and both variant-effect scoring and genome design applications.
notes: Trained across all domains of life rather than one clade, so `organism` carries the local term `multi-species` -- no single NCBITaxon node says this without claiming a specific clade. Two parameter variants ship together as one release, carried as the 7B-40B range rather than collapsed to a single figure.

name: ExPecto
description: We developed a deep learning-based framework, ExPecto, that can accurately predict, ab initio from a DNA sequence, the tissue-specific transcriptional effects of mutations, including those that are rare or that have not been observed.

name: Feng 2025 Benchmarking DNA foundation
description: Here, we present a benchmarking study of three recent DNA foundation language models, including DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer version-2 (NT-v2), and HyenaDNA, focusing on the quality of their zero-shot embeddings across a diverse range of genomic tasks and species through analyses of 57 real datasets.

name: Flashzoi
description: Re-implementation of Borzoi substituting rotary positional encodings and FlashAttention-2 for relative positional encodings, giving over 3-fold faster training and inference and up to 2.4-fold lower memory use while maintaining or improving accuracy.
notes: A port under its own name, so a separate entity with `variant_of` rather than a Borzoi link -- the granularity rule's worked case. Weights for all four Flashzoi and Borzoi replicates are published together under MIT; the replicates are one entity, not four. Licensed more permissively than Borzoi itself, which matters for downstream reuse.

name: Foster 2021 Contrastive Mixture Posteriors
description: We propose the Contrastive Mixture of Posteriors (CoMP) method that uses a novel misalignment penalty defined in terms of mixtures of the variational posteriors to enforce this independence in latent space.

name: Francesco 2026 Differentiable Retrieval-Augmented Generation
description: We introduce PT-RAG (Perturbation-aware Two-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a plug-in retrieval-and-conditioning module for generative cellular perturbation response.

name: Fu 2026 Benchmarking gene expression
description: Here, we introduce ReconEval, a benchmark for evaluating gene expression reconstruction from single-cell latent spaces.

name: GEARS
description: Graph neural network predicting transcriptional outcomes of multigene perturbations, including combinations never seen in training, by combining a gene co-expression graph with a knowledge graph of gene ontology relations.
notes: Deliberately shallow. Perturbation modelling is covered properly by the Stegle group's living catalogue (>152 methods, Nat Rev Genet 2026) and CFCR points outward rather than competing -- see the `website` link. GEARS is here as the representative entry so the `what` axis is not empty, not as the start of a perturbation index. `architecture` required a new vocabulary term: GNN is absent from the schema §3.1 enum, and it is the dominant architecture on this axis.

name: GenART
description: We present GenART, a genomic language model framework that dynamically segments DNA into variable-length words directly from raw sequences without manual annotation.

name: GeneJepa
description: We introduce G ene J epa , a self-supervised foundation model that learns a predictive world model of single-cell transcriptomes.

name: GenomeHarness
description: We present GenomeHarness, an agentic harness for adapting genome language models through controlled search over fine-tuning recipes.

name: gReLU
description: Here we present gReLU, a comprehensive software framework that enables advanced sequence modeling pipelines, including data preprocessing, modeling, evaluation, interpretation, variant effect prediction and regulatory element design.

name: Hacisuleyman 2026 Rapid interpretable protein
description: Here, we present a template-based pattern- matching approach that predicts protein contact maps by identifying conserved structural motifs from homologous experimental structures.

name: Hang 2025 Puget predicts gene
description: We present Puget, a deep learning model that predicts cell type-specific gene expression from sequence and Hi-C data, which captures 3D chromatin organization.

name: Hanson 2018 Accurate prediction protein
description: Here, we propose a novel protein contact map prediction method by stacking residual convolutional networks with two-dimensional residual bidirectional recurrent LSTM networks, and using both one-dimensional sequence-based and two- dimensional evolutionary coupling-based information.

name: Honig 2024 Long-range gene expression
description: We introduce Genetic sequence Token Alignment (GTA), which aligns genetic sequence features with natural language tokens, allowing for symbolic reasoning of genomic sequence features via the frozen language model.

name: Hu 2024 Benchmarking algorithms single-cell
description: Here, we present a benchmark study of 14 protein abundance/chromatin accessibility prediction algorithms and 18 single-cell multi-omics integration algorithms using 47 single- cell multi-omics datasets.

name: HyCoSeq
description: We propose HyCoSeq, a contextual hyperbolic representation learning framework for genomic sequences.

name: Javed 2025 multi-modal transformer cell
description: Here, we present EpiBERT, a multi-modal transformer that learns generalizable representations of genomic sequence and cell type-specific chromatin accessibility through a masked accessibility-based pre-training objective.

name: Jiang 2025 Evaluating DNA function
description: We introduce a benchmark called Nullsettes, which assesses how well models can predict in silico loss-of-function (LOF) mutations, in synthetic expression cassettes with little evolutionary precedent.

name: Karimzadeh 2026 high-resolution protein-RNA binding
description: Here we introduce eclair CLIP (ecCLIP), a high-throughput CLIP-seq platform that combines endogenous protein tagging for uniform affinity capture with ligation-free library preparation to generate high-resolution RNA-protein binding profiles.

name: Kathail 2024 Leveraging genomic deep
description: We describe practical considerations for making such predictions and categorize the types of ground truth data used to evaluate variant effect predictions, providing insight into the settings in which current models are most useful.

name: Li 2026 comparison single-cell perturbation
description: We present a large-scale benchmark of 13 representative methods and baselines across 25 datasets spanning diverse perturbation modalities and species, including two primary immune-cell drug-response resources.

name: Li 2026 Deep Learning-Guided Identification
description: We developed ZEN-former (Zebrafish EN-former), an Enformer-based sequence- to-function model trained on neuronal subclass chromatin accessibility profiles from the adult mouse brain.

name: Li 2026 mechanism-annotated benchmark reveals
description: Here we present scDrugPerturb-Bench, a mechanism-annotated benchmark that links matched control and drug-treated single-cell RNA- sequencing profiles to literature-curated directional key-gene evidence.

name: Liang 2026 split-control criterion few-shot
description: We introduce SafeDelta, a split-control criterion that uses calibration data to decide whether to adapt.

name: Lingshu-Cell
description: Here, we introduce Lingshu-Cell, a masked discrete diffusion model that learns transcriptomic state distributions and supports conditional simulation under perturbation.

name: Liu 2026 Predicting cell-state-specific gene
description: We developed Bolero, a sequence-to-function model whose parameters condition on atlas-scale cell-state embeddings and additional biological variables to predict cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance from DNA.

name: Long 2026 Learning Perturbation Effects
description: Here, we introduce PertOmni, a CLIP-style multimodal representation-learning framework that aligns transcriptomic perturbation signatures with text-derived embeddings of curated genes and compound descriptions, as well as image- derived embeddings from cell paintings.

name: Lorch 2026 Latent Causal Diffusions
description: Here, we present the latent causal diffusion (LCD), a generative model that frames single-cell gene expression as a stationary diffusion process observed under measurement noise.

name: Lu 2026 Generative Virtual Tissue
description: Here, we introduce the Cell Interaction Foundation Model (CIFM), a virtual tissue model that forward-simulates the transcriptional dynamics of cells in human tissue under arbitrary therapeutic conditions based upon a spatial transcriptomic seed.

name: LucaCell
description: Here we present LucaCell, a sequence-centric foundation model that represents genes through pre-trained mRNA sequence embeddings rather than static gene annotations.

name: Maddu 2026 Learning biophysical gene
description: Here we introduce Probability Flow Matching (PFM), a scalable framework for learning biophysically consistent stochastic processes directly from time-resolved single-cell measurements.

name: MAP
description: We present MAP , a framework that integrates structured biological knowledge into cellular perturbation modeling and supports zero-shot prediction for small molecules with scarce or absent perturbation profiles.

name: McAnany 2026 Positional interpretation cis-regulatory
description: Here, we introduce pairwise influence by sequence attribution (PISA), which uses attribution to combinatorially decode which bases contributed to the readout at a specific genomic coordinate.

name: Meng 2026 multi-tissue epigenomic atlas
description: Here we present SheepEpimap, a multi-tissue regulatory atlas harmonizing 516 CUT&Tag histone modifications, ATAC- seq, and RNA-seq datasets across 43 adult tissues in sheep.

name: Molina 2026 Perturbation response decomposition
description: We introduce a decomposition framework that explicitly separates transcriptional responses into global, perturbation-specific, cell-line-specific, and perturbation-by-cell-line interaction components.

name: MultiPert
description: Here, we present MultiPert, a deep learning framework specifically designed for predicting perturbation responses in single-cell multi-omics data.

name: Navidi 2025 Adaptive resampling machine
description: We present a generalizable Adaptive Resampling (AR) approach that addresses these limitations and enhances single-cell representation learning by resampling data based on its learned latent structure in an online, adaptive manner concurrent with model training.

name: Nemecek 2026 Quantifying Memorization Privacy
description: We present a comprehensive, multi-vector privacy evaluation framework designed to quantify memorization risks in GLMs.

name: Nguyen 2025 Sequence-based chromatin activity
description: Here, we present a deep learning-based framework that utilizes functional genomic data to generate genome-wide predictions of the regulatory impact of noncoding variants in cattle, chicken, pig, and Atlantic salmon.

name: Nucleotide Transformer
description: Family of transformer DNA language models pretrained on human and multi-species genomes, released as a set of checkpoints from 50M to 2.5B parameters and evaluated by probing on downstream regulatory tasks.
notes: The `open-weights` case, and the reason that tier is distinct from `open-source`: inference code is on GitHub, but the published checkpoints carry CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, which forbids commercial use and imposes share-alike on derivatives. Anyone building a product on this needs to read the license before the paper. Checkpoint sizes span two orders of magnitude, which is what `n_parameters_min`/`_max` exist to carry: the entity is the family, not one checkpoint, so filtering on size means filtering on the range.

name: Onawole 2026 Trust-Aware Sequence-to-Function Modelling
description: We develop and evaluate RegTrust-XAI, a trust-aware framework separating these questions using three inference-time signals: ensemble consensus, motif-grounded attribution coherence, and applicability-domain distance.

name: Oyster
description: We introduce Oyster, the first convolutional architecture that can be toggled between Exact (ignoring associations) and non-Exact modes.

name: PARNET
description: Here we introduce Parnet, an RNA foundation model trained directly and exclusively on experimental CLIP-seq data.

name: Passow 2026 Amplicon Protein Bead
description: Here, we present Amplicon/Protein Bead Display (APB-Display), which expresses and purifies >100,000 protein variants in vitro in 1 day.

name: Pearce 2026 Interpretable variant effect
description: We introduce a covariance-based probe that captures second- order structure from Evo 2 sequence embeddings to predict variant pathogenicity across variant types and functional consequences, matching or exceeding specialized predictors within their domains.

name: PertDiffBench
description: Here we introduce PertDiffBench, a standardized benchmark for diffusion-based transcriptomic perturbation prediction across single-cell and bulk RNA- seq datasets.

name: PerturbBridge
description: We propose PerturbBridge, a conditional latent Schrödinger Bridge framework that reformulates stochastic population transport over high-dimensional, sparse geneexpression profiles as bridge learning in a compact cell latent space.

name: Poisoning the Genome
description: We present the first systematic study of training data poisoning in genomic language models, targeting both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

name: Radig 2025 Tracking biological hallucinations
description: Here, we present scArchon, a reproducible, modular benchmarking platform built on Snakemake, designed to evaluate perturbation response prediction tools in an unbiased and extensible manner.

name: Ramarao-Milne 2026 Evaluating cross-species transferability
description: We developed a scoring-approach for AI-agents to autonomously assess AlphaGenome prediction confidence and accurately differentiate between AlphaGenome’s robust sequence-level recognition across species and its current limitations when interpreting un-fine-mapped regulatory variants.

name: Rather 2026 Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific
description: Here, we develop Kidzoi, a kidney cell-type-specific S2F model obtained by transfer learning from the pretrained model Borzoi using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data from human kidney tissue.

name: RegFM
description: Here we present RegFM, a context- aware foundation model for human transcriptional regulation.

name: SCALE
description: We present SCALE, a conditional transport model that represents cells as unordered sets and predicts treated populations without cell-level matching.

name: ScAPE
description: We present ScAPE (Single Cell Analysis of Perturbational Effects), an ML method for predicting drug-induced gene expression changes.

name: scBasset
description: Here we introduce scBasset, a sequence-based convolutional neural network method to model scATAC data.

name: Schmauch 2025 deep learning-based multiscale
description: Here, we present a deep learning-based approach for multiscale integration of spTx with tumor morphology (MISO).

name: scooby
description: Here, we introduce scooby, the first framework to model scRNA-seq coverage and scATAC-seq insertion profiles along the genome from sequence at single-cell resolution.

name: Serizay 2025 Multi-modal data integration
description: Here, we present momics, a unified framework to consolidate multi-omics data in a single repository and interrogate it with a high-performance query engine.

name: Sigliano 2026 Metric-Calibrated Replay Single-Cell
description: We present TCPE, a metric-calibrated replay framework that makes scorer orientation, top-k response restriction, seed aggregation, and reference-margin comparison explicit components of a benchmark statement.

name: Signals in the Cells
description: We present four tasks for contextual learning at single-cell resolution: drug-target nomination, genetic perturbation response prediction, chemical perturbation response prediction, and protein-peptide interaction prediction.

name: SLIM
description: Here we present SLIM, a lightweight extension of the bilinear model of Ahlmann-Eltze et al. SLIM represents perturbations with 64-dimensional embeddings derived from the STRING protein network and predicts mean transcriptional responses through a closed-form ridge-regression estimator.

name: SpliSync
description: We developed SpliSync, a genomic language model-driven method for splice site correction that integrates a pre-trained genomic sequence model (HyenaDNA), alignment data, and a U-net architecture to predict splice sites at nucleotide resolution.

name: SPOT-Contact-LM
description: Here, we developed a contact-map predictor utilizing the output of a pre-trained language model ESM-1b as an input along with a large training set and an ensemble of residual neural networks.

name: SPOT-Contact-Single
description: Here, we developed a contact-map predictor utilizing the output of a pre-trained language model ESM-1b as an input along with a large training set and an ensemble of residual neural networks.

name: STAMPS
description: We present STAMPS (Signal-peptide Transformer for Augmenting Mammalian Protein Secretion), a generative, autoregressive transformer fine-tuned on ∼6,000 mammalian signal peptides to design de novo sequences that modulate and enhance secretion across proteins and hosts.

name: Starr 2025 detect positive selection
description: Here, we propose that these methods can be considered special cases of a more general framework to detect positive selection with any variant effect prediction method.

name: Stochastic Flow Map for Count Data
description: We propose Count Flow Map, a generative model that learns finite-time transitions directly in count space for one- or few-step generation.

name: Sugimoto 2026 transcription factor regulatory
description: Here, we present TFActProfiler, a TF-mRNA resource and computational framework that learns signed, quantitative TF-mRNA regulatory coefficients by integrating heterogeneous prior evidence (ChIP-based, motif-based, and curated TF-mRNA annotations) with large-scale bulk and single-cell RNA-seq atlases.

name: Sun 2025 Hi-Compass resolves cell-type
description: We present Hi- Compass, a generalizable deep learning model that accurately predicts chromatin organization across diverse biological contexts, from bulk to single-cell samples.

name: Sun 2026 Pretraining Enhances Megabase-Scale
description: Here we introduce GB.GeneUnet, an 837M-parameter transformer-based U-Net pretrained on 6 trillion tokens from multi-species genomes in OpenGenome2, extending genomic context to 1 Mb with up to 100× inference speedup over GeneMoE, a preliminary MoE transformer baseline of similar model size pretrained on the same data.

name: Torghabeh 2026 Genomic language improve
description: Here, we developed deep learning sequence-to-expression (S2E) models that leverage context- aware sequence embeddings from the PlantCaduceus genomic language model instead of one-hot encoding of sequences, to predict gene expression across 17 plant species.

name: Toward Interpretable and Generalizable AI in Regulatory Genomics
V3Cell
description: Here we introduce V3Cell, a vision-guided framework that constructs in silico surrogates of organoids directly from non-invasive bright-field microscopy.

name: VariantFormer
description: Here, we present VariantFormer, a 1.2-billion-parameter transformer that predicts gene-level RNA abundance directly from personalized diploid genomes.

name: VCLMU
description: We introduce a mechanism-centric virtual cell world model that represents cellular state as a set of Latent Mechanism Units (LMUs) and treats genetic perturbations as actions on these latent states.

name: Wei 2026 Benchmarking algorithms single-cell
description: Here, we present a comprehensive benchmark of 27 methods for single-cell perturbation response prediction, evaluated across 29 datasets using 6 complementary performance metrics.

name: Wei 2026 CAPRA predicts single-cell
description: Here we introduce Control-Anchored Perturbation Residual Architecture (CAPRA), a response-anchored model for genetic perturbation prediction.

name: XChrom
description: Here, we present XChrom, a deep learning framework for genome-wide cross-cell chromatin accessibility prediction that integrates genomic sequence and single- cell transcriptomics-derived cell identity into a unified model.

name: Yu 2026 FP8 Inference Genomic
description: We present an empirical case study of FP8 post-training quantization applied to GenomeOcean, a computationally efficient genomic foundation model with strong reported performance across diverse genomics tasks [Zhou et al., 2025].

name: Zeng 2022 Spatial transcriptomics prediction
description: Here, we developed Hist2ST, a deep learning-based model to predict RNA-seq expression from histology images.

name: Zhang 2026 Generation-Powered Inference Distribution-Valued
description: We propose generation-powered inference (GPI), a general framework for improving inference on distribution-valued parameters using auxiliary generative models.

name: Zhang 2026 Hierarchical refinements cis-regulatory
description: Here we introduce a two-stage selective framework (TSSF) that performs hierarchical refinements: nucleotide-level masking within each cCRE, followed by cCRE-level selection around each gene, implemented with information-bottleneck priors and a fully Transformer-based architecture.

name: Zhang 2026 Highly accurate ab
description: Here we introduce ANNEVO, a mixture of experts-based genomic language model that directly models distal sequence dependencies and joint evolutionary relationships from diverse genomes, enabling precise ab initio gene annotation.

name: Zhong 2026 Perturbation Curve continuous
description: Here, we present Perturbation Curve (PertCurve), a nonlinear, curve-based computational framework that models the trajectories of transcriptomic responses by explicitly incorporating diverse perturbation magnitudes and strengths.

name: Zhu 2026 structured cross-condition prediction
description: We introduce TranScouter, a lightweight encoderdecoder framework that represents perturbed genes using LLM- derived embeddings of their text summaries and represents biological conditions using transcriptomic profiles of control cells from the target condition.

name: DelRosso 2023 human transcriptional effector domains
description: Large-scale mapping and systematic mutagenesis of human transcriptional effector domains by HT-recruit, establishing sequence determinants of activation and repression across a broad survey of annotated domains.
notes: The mutagenesis arm is what distinguishes this from a pure discovery screen: it reports which residues matter, not only which domains work, which is the difference between a parts list and a design rule. `n_records` is null -- the domain count is reported across several screen arms in the paper and was not confirmable from open metadata.

name: EpiFactors 2022 epigenetic regulators
description: Curated database of human epigenetic regulators, protein complexes and their functional annotation, covering chromatin-modifying enzymes, remodelers and reader domains.
notes: Curated annotation rather than a screen, so `dominant_validation_level` is `predicted` -- the entries are literature-asserted functional assignments, not measurements in a recruitment assay. That difference is exactly what the validation-level vocabulary exists to carry, and it matters when picking a chromatin remodeler to build an eCR from.

name: Fernández 2019 Transmembrane Prolines Mediate
description: Here, we report that individual replacement of prolines in DesKs TM1 and TM5 helices by alanine (DesKPA) locked DesK in a phosphatase-ON state, abrogating membrane fluidity responses.

name: Morita 2020 Synergistic Upregulation Target
description: Here we describe the screening of factors that exhibit the best synergistic activation of gene expression with TET1 in the dCas9-SunTag format.

name: Partridge 2020 Occupancy maps 208
description: Here we present, as part of the ENCODE (Encyclopedia of DNA Elements) project, data and analyses from chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by high-throughput sequencing (ChIP-seq) experiments using the human HepG2 cell line for 208 chromatin-associated proteins (CAPs).

name: Plaper 2020 Coiled-coil heterodimers increased
description: Here, we report the design and versatile applications of orthogonal CC dimer-forming peptides with a dissociation constant in the low nanomolar range.

name: Sonn 2025 MeCP2 interacts super
description: We propose a previously unknown mechanism by which MePC2 regulates gene expression underlying synaptic plasticity.

name: Strobel 2020 High-throughput identification synthetic
description: Here we describe a fast and broadly applicable method to functionally screen complex riboswitch libraries (~1.8 × 10 4 constructs) by cDNA-amplicon-sequencing in transiently transfected and stimulated human cells.

name: Takahashi 2019 Cell Assays SINEUP
description: Here, we present a method to selectively up-regulate protein expression of desired genes in cultured cells by means of synthetic antisense non-coding RNAs known as SINEUPs.

name: Tikhmyanova 2017 Small molecule perturbation
description: We propose that C60 perturbs the normal interaction and function of CAND1 with Cullins to promote the stabilization of substrates like ZTA and p53, leading to EBV reactivation from latency.

name: Tycko 2025 compact effector domains
description: HT-recruit screen of compact activation and repression domains measured across multiple cellular contexts; 38 CD2 activation domains and 1,223 CD43 repression domains.
notes: `year: 2024` is the verified Nature Biotechnology issue year. The collection is known in the lab as "Tycko 2025" and `ecr_lib_source_key: Tycko_2025` is kept unchanged because it is the join key into eCR_mod_lib's `source_screen` column -- changing it would break the deep link for cosmetic consistency.

name: Weber 2019 PiggyBac transposon tools
description: Here, we describe PiggyBac transposon tools and mouse models for recessive screening and show their application to study clonal B-cell lymphomagenesis.

name: ATAC-seq
description: We describe an assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq), based on direct in vitro transposition of sequencing adaptors into native chromatin, as a rapid and sensitive method for integrative epigenomic analysis.

name: CUT&Tag
description: Here we describe Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag), an enzyme-tethering strategy that provides efficient high- resolution sequencing libraries for profiling diverse chromatin components.

name: CUT&RUN targeted in situ genome-wide profiling
description: The reference CUT&RUN protocol for targeted in situ chromatin profiling at high efficiency from low cell numbers, hosted on protocols.io by the originating lab.
notes: The `external` origin case, and the model for how protocols should be catalogued: a real protocols.io DOI, maintained by the authors, versioned upstream. CFCR adds discovery and trust metadata, nothing else.

name: Low-input CUT&RUN for sorted MEF populations
description: CUT&RUN adapted for 5,000-20,000 sorted cells, optimized for histone marks during MEF reprogramming timecourses.
notes: The `cfc-lab` origin case. `protocol_doi` is null: schema §9 shows 10.17504/protocols.io.xxxxx, which is a placeholder, and no real DOI has been minted yet. This entity is therefore the one seed record that will fail the "every entity has a primary paper" QC check -- it is the whitelisted exception the check needs to support, since an unpublished in-house protocol has no paper by definition.

name: Omni-ATAC
description: We present Omni-ATAC, an improved ATAC-seq protocol for chromatin accessibility profiling that works across multiple applications with substantial improvement of signal-to-background ratio and information content.
